The evaluation job failed\\n\\n- **Read the job\\'s `FailureReason`, then the log group `/aws/sagemaker/TrainingJobs`** \u2014 AWS names that log group for Nova evaluation job errors (LLM-SM-EVAL-002) ([Nova evaluation troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/nova-model-evaluation.html)).\\n- **`RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed`** typically means the checkpoint in `model_name_or_path` does not match `model_type` (for example a Nova 2.0 Lite checkpoint evaluated with a 1.0 model type) (LLM-SM-EVAL-002) ([Nova evaluation troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/nova-model-evaluation.html)).\\n- **Bring-your-own-dataset runs need exactly one file named `gen_qa.jsonl`**, in an S3 location the training job can read, with `query` and `response` on every line (`system`, `images`, `metadata` optional); only one `.jsonl` is allowed and it must follow the schema strictly (LLM-SM-EVAL-002) ([Nova evaluation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/nova-model-evaluation.html)).\\n- **Access to the dataset and output paths is the job\\'s execution role**: an evaluation runs as a training job, so the `CreateTrainingJob` execution role needs read on the input prefix, write on the output path and `kms:Decrypt` for SSE-KMS input (LLM-SM-EVAL-002) ([CreateTrainingJob execution role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html)).\\n\\n## 2. The job cannot start on an instance limit\\n\\n- **`ResourceLimitExceeded` is an account resource limit** for the training instance the evaluation uses; request an increase through Service Quotas ([CreateTrainingJob errors](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_CreateTrainingJob.html), [quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/regions-quotas.html)).\\n\\n## 3. {"id": "90a00e50-40b5-410a-b058-058104fdc33c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Short answer:** the job's failure reason says the job couldn't read the dataset, and `AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess` doesn't cover the KMS half of that read. Your description points to a missing KMS permission, but I can't confirm that from here.

**What the failure reason shows**

- The job couldn't read `s3://eval-bucket/nova/benchmark.jsonl` and got `AccessDenied`.
- It doesn't say whether S3 or KMS denied the request, so I can't name the cause from the message alone.

**The gap in what you described**

- A Nova evaluation runs as a SageMaker training job. AWS documents that the execution role needs read access on the input prefix, write access on the output path, and `kms:Decrypt` for SSE-KMS input.
- `AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess` grants S3 actions only. It includes no KMS permissions.
- Reading an object encrypted with a customer managed key therefore needs `kms:Decrypt` in two places: the role's identity policy, and the key policy (or a grant) that allows the role. The key policy has to allow it even if the role's policy does.
- If the role has `kms:Decrypt` through another policy and the key policy allows it, this isn't the cause and you'd look further.

**How to confirm**

1. Check the role the job actually used. The `RoleArn` is in `DescribeTrainingJob`. It can differ from the role you inspected.
2. Look for `kms:Decrypt` on that role, scoped to the bucket's key ARN. Then check that the key policy allows the role directly or through IAM delegation.
3. Check the bucket policy and any VPC endpoint policy for explicit denies on this role or prefix.
4. Open the CloudWatch log group `/aws/sagemaker/TrainingJobs`. AWS names it for Nova evaluation errors, and it may show whether the denial came from S3 or KMS.
5. In CloudTrail, look for a `kms:Decrypt` `AccessDenied` from the role around the failure time. That would settle it.

**A separate problem to fix before you rerun**

- For bring-your-own-dataset runs, AWS requires exactly one file named `gen_qa.jsonl` in the S3 location. Every line needs `query` and `response` fields.
- Your path ends in `benchmark.jsonl`. If this is a bring-your-own-dataset recipe, rename or re-point the file, or the job will fail again after the access issue is fixed.
- If you're using a built-in benchmark rather than your own data, ignore this.

I can't change IAM or KMS permissions, so the role and key policy changes would be yours to make. If you paste the role's attached policies, the key policy, and the CloudWatch log lines around the failure, I can go through them with you.

Sources: [Nova evaluation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/nova-model-evaluation.html) and [SageMaker execution roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html).", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
